utterances.text: Is it correct that those zones of responsibilities were established through orders to those brigades there in Central Bosnia by Colonel Blaskic who was the commander of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Kovacic please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Could anybody else issue orders to them in this zone?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that there were exceptional situations? For example, the BH army would attack, your line would fall, and then in the -- in your zone of responsibility where the Viteska Brigade was, any unit would come to help you?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The last document that we saw now, isn't that precisely that kind of a situation?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is that kind of a situation, but it is also obvious how it ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Well, never mind. But this did not end.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that from time to time, it is precisely this help, this overlapping. We have two units in the same place at the same time that led to various misunderstandings in terms of the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It led to misunderstandings very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Is it correct -- let me just -- is it correct that the order that was shown to you, Z997.2, that it actually regulates that particular matter because it uses the term that shows that? In the introduction, it points out the problem that is in question.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that this introduction actually shows that it was overlapping?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, that is what was shown.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Kovacic please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You are being asked to slow down, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Let us just go back to the order that we've been dealing with for quite sometime, and that is being brought into question. This is the famous order of 1.30 at night on the 16th of April. We discussed it at length. I think that you don't even have to be shown this order anymore because I think you've had it in front of you for hours. If necessary, I am going to show it to you.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that in point one, in paragraph one, it says Vranjska, Kruscica, and that this is the possible direction from which an attack may come?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: This paragraph one, does it give the possibility of any different kind of interpretation to illiterate or an illiterate soldier when he reads that paragraph one?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is crystal clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Paragraph two now explains in greater detail what the activities -- what the activities that the unit has to undertake in order to carry out the order from paragraph one; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you notice that there is a small sentence on the left-hand side by the margin that says Donja Veceriska. There is Veceriska, Donja Veceriska, and Vranjska?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: It is correct that in no other place in the text of this order does the author go back to Veceriska and to the task concerning Veceriska?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So it is only in paragraph two that Vranjska and Kruscica are mentioned in terms of the elaboration of this task?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In one sentence, please, a layman soldier or an average soldier like the ones you had in the brigade, if he had got that kind of order, that is to say, someone below you, what would his understanding have been of this order?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His understanding would have been, for example, if he was a squad leader, that with his men, he should go to the territory ordered, the area ordered, and to carry out the other points of the order. If the order says Vranjska and Kruscica, then of course he's not going to go elsewhere. He knows very well where that is. Also all soldiers know that very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do we agree it is quite clear even for an average soldier?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Just two minor points now, or rather only one. The Prosecutor on the 19th of July, a few days ago, tendered document Z1406.1. That document, I'm going to describe it to you now, was introduced during the testimony of a protected witness. I'm saying this for the Court now, that was Witness DL. I'm going to read a sentence to you now because we don't have enough time to get the document out right now. But let me describe it so that it will be clear what I'm talking about. That is a document dated the 21st of March, 1994, and it is entitled, "Office of National Security of the Republic of Croatia." It is addressed to Dr. Franjo Tudjman. The subject is massacre in Ahmici. It is signed by the director of HIS. It says Doctor -- Professor Miroslav Tudjman in print, I think I've described it sufficiently. And in this document, inter alia, there is the following sentence, "It can be said with certitude that Mario Cerkez is not involved in the massacre in the village of Ahmici and that he did not have any influence on the events themselves." Witness Sajevic, do you agree with this kind of statement?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you ever have a different opinion in this regard?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have thus concluded. I just wish to draw the attention of the Trial Chamber to one thing. I'm not going to argue, but let us just bear this in mind. This document was drawn up considerably before the indictment against Mario Cerkez was written. I'm just saying this for the sake of authenticity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You can make all those points in your submissions and no doubt you will. Major Sajevic, thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give your evidence. It is now concluded. You are free to go. And the Chamber will sit tomorrow morning at half past 9.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 28th day of July, 2000, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.27 p.m.,
